title: Reciprocal polynomial of a polynomial with constant term one
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $P(T)=\sum_{k=0}^{r}c_kT^k\in R[T]$ with $c_0=P(0)=1$ and $c_r\neq0$, so that $r=\deg P$. Define the reciprocal polynomial

$$
P^\#(U)=U^{r}P(U^{-1}):=\sum_{k=0}^{r}c_kU^{r-k}\in R[U].
$$

Then:

1. $P^\#$ is monic of degree $r$, and $P^\#(0)=c_r$.
2. Let $\varphi:R\to K$ be a ring homomorphism into a field $K$ with $\varphi(c_r)\neq0$ (for instance any injective $\varphi$; for $R=\mathbf Z$, the unique homomorphism into any field $K$ of characteristic $0$), and write $\varphi(Q)$ for the coefficientwise extension of $Q\in R[T]$. Then $\deg\varphi(P)=r$, $\varphi(P)(0)=1$, and $\varphi(P^\#)=(\varphi(P))^\#$.
3. For $\varphi$ as in (2) and $x\in K$: $\varphi(P^\#)(x)=0$ if and only if $x\neq0$ and $\varphi(P)(x^{-1})=0$. Equivalently, $\varphi(P^\#)(x)=x^{r}\,\varphi(P)(x^{-1})$ for $x\neq0$, and $\varphi(P^\#)(0)=\varphi(c_r)\neq0$. In particular the roots of $\varphi(P^\#)$ in $K$ are exactly the inverses of the roots of $\varphi(P)$ in $K$, and all of them are nonzero.

proof.text:
Clause (2), degree and constant term. The coefficient of $T^k$ in $\varphi(P)$ is $\varphi(c_k)$. Since $\varphi(c_r)
eq0$ and $\varphi(c_k)=\varphi(0)=0$ for $k>r$, $\deg\varphi(P)=r$ with leading coefficient $\varphi(c_r)$; and $\varphi(P)(0)=\varphi(c_0)=\varphi(1)=1$. So $\varphi(P)$ satisfies the hypotheses of the statement over $K$ (constant term $1$, nonzero coefficient in degree $r=\deg$), and $(\varphi(P))^\#$ is defined with the same $r$. The hypothesis $\varphi(c_r)
eq0$ holds for injective $\varphi$ because $c_r
eq0$, and for $R=\mathbf Z$ and $K$ of characteristic $0$ because then $\varphi$ is injective [lem-weil-integers-injective-char-zero]. (Mathlib: `Polynomial.natDegree_map_of_leadingCoeff_ne_zero`, `Polynomial.leadingCoeff_map_of_leadingCoeff_ne_zero`, `Polynomial.coeff_map`, `map_one`.)

proof.text: Clause (2), extension commutes with $\#$. By step 1 applied over $R$, the coefficient of $U^j$ in $\varphi(P^\#)$ is $\varphi(c_{r-j})$ for $j\le r$ and $\varphi(0)=0$ for $j>r$; by step 1 applied over $K$ to $\varphi(P)$, whose degree is $r$ and whose coefficients are $\varphi(c_k)$ (step 3), the coefficient of $U^j$ in $(\varphi(P))^\#$ is the same. Hence $\varphi(P^\#)=(\varphi(P))^\#$. (Mathlib: `Polynomial.reflect_map` at $N=r$ together with `Polynomial.natDegree_map_of_leadingCoeff_ne_zero`; this needs only $\varphi(c_r)\neq0$, whereas the source repository's `Polynomial.reverse_map` in WeilConjectures/Mathlib/Algebra/Polynomial/Reverse.lean assumes $\varphi$ injective; Mathlib has no `reverse_map`.)

proof.text: Clause (3), values. Let $x\in K$. By step 4 and step 1, $\varphi(P^\#)(x)=\sum_{k=0}^r\varphi(c_k)x^{r-k}$. If $x=0$, every term with $k<r$ vanishes and $\varphi(P^\#)(0)=\varphi(c_r)\neq0$. If $x\neq0$, $x$ is invertible in the field $K$ and $\sum_k\varphi(c_k)x^{r-k}=x^r\sum_k\varphi(c_k)(x^{-1})^k=x^r\,\varphi(P)(x^{-1})$. (Mathlib: `Polynomial.eval₂_reverse_mul_pow` with `Invertible x⁻¹` from `invertibleOfNonzero`, read with $x^{-1}$ in place of $x$; `Polynomial.coeff_zero_eq_eval_zero` with `Polynomial.coeff_zero_reverse` for $x=0$.)
